about: cdk-nag (AwsSolutionsChecks) findings recorded once at VIB-65. Every entry names one construct path and one rule id, with the reason the finding is accepted. A new finding fails `cdk synth` and the infra tests: fix the construct, or add an entry here with a real reason. A stale entry (its construct or finding is gone) fails tests/integration/infra/guardrails.test.ts.

suppressions.reason: Recorded at the VIB-65 baseline: the VPC has no flow logs yet. Ingress reaches only the ALB through CloudFront's origin-facing prefix list, and the database subnets are isolated. Adding flow logs is a cost decision for the operator, not a lint fix.
The ECS tasks read DB_PASSWORD from this secret only at start, so an automatic rotation would break running tasks until they restart. Rotation is a manual runbook step (docs/deploy-registry-aws.md).
Rotating the Better Auth session secret signs every console user out, so it is rotated by hand from the runbook (docs/deploy-registry-aws.md section 1.5), never on a timer.

This secret encrypts the jwks rows at rest. A timed rotation would leave those rows sealed under a key the registry no longer holds; it is rotated by hand from the runbook (docs/deploy-registry-aws.md section 1.5).

Every sealed row must be resealed under a new vault key (the ResealTask, apps/registry README 'Rotating the vault key'). A Secrets Manager timed rotation would replace the key without resealing and make sealed rows unreadable.
Postgres listens on 5432 inside isolated subnets and accepts only the service's security group. A non-default port adds no protection there and would break the self-host recipe's defaults.

Recorded at the VIB-65 baseline: CloudFront access logs are off. The registry logs every request itself (one completion line per request with a request id), and CloudFront logs would hold client IPs and paths the privacy rules keep out of logs.
The registry serves customers in every country, so the distribution has no geo restriction on purpose.
Recorded at the VIB-65 baseline: no WAF web ACL yet. Adding one is a cost and operations decision for the operator, not a lint fix.
Recorded at the VIB-65 baseline: ALB access logs are off. The registry writes one completion line per request, and ALB logs would hold client IPs and query strings the privacy rules keep out of logs.

The plain environment variables are non-secret settings (mode, base URL, hostnames, ports, paths, the public OIDC client id). Every credential reaches the container through ECS Secrets from Secrets Manager, which tests/integration/infra/registry-stack.test.ts asserts.
Same as the service task: the plain environment variables are non-secret settings, and every credential comes from Secrets Manager through ECS Secrets.
CDK's generated execution-role policy grants ecr:GetAuthorizationToken, which AWS defines only on Resource '*'. Every other action in it is scoped to the repository, log group and secret ARNs.
Same as the service task: ecr:GetAuthorizationToken exists only on Resource '*'. The other actions are scoped to ARNs.
ec2:DescribeManagedPrefixLists has no resource-level permissions, so AWS accepts it only on Resource '*'. It is read-only and looks up CloudFront's origin-facing prefix list.

CDK's own LogRetention singleton Lambda sets retention on log groups whose names are known only at deploy time; its policy (logs:PutRetentionPolicy, logs:DeleteRetentionPolicy) is generated by aws-cdk-lib.
CDK's own LogRetention singleton Lambda attaches AWSLambdaBasicExecutionRole so it can write its own logs. aws-cdk-lib generates the role; this app does not choose its policies.
CDK's AwsCustomResource singleton Lambda (the prefix-list lookup) attaches AWSLambdaBasicExecutionRole so it can write its own logs. aws-cdk-lib generates the role.
